newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse to lengthen sessions from January 2.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse to lengthen sessions from January 2.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse will lengthen its sessions by an hour and a half from January 2, with sessions lasting from 1100 until 1430 local time, PAP news agency quoted the exchange's president as saying on Wednesday.
Currently Warsaw bourse sessions take place from 1100 to 1300.
Exchange president Wieslaw Rozlucki said continuous trade would begin after the regular single-price-auction session ended instead of the two running concurrently.
For stocks trading in both systems the price at the single-price-auction system would be the starting point for the continuous trade system.
According to the change, the regular bourse session would begin at 1100 local time and end at 1200. Continuous trade would begin at 1230.
PAP said the order-balancing session would be shortened to a maximum of 40 minutes from 45 minutes and would last from 1120 to 1200.
